did_you_know.text: Did you know? The people of Kiriath-jearim brought the ark of the LORD to the house of Abinadab on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar son of Abinadab to guard it.
Did you know? The ark of the LORD remained at Kiriath-jearim for twenty years, and during that time all Israel yearned for the LORD.
Did you know? Samuel urged the Israelites to remove the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth, commit their hearts to the LORD, and serve him alone.
Did you know? The Israelites gathered at Mizpah, drew water and poured it out before the LORD, fasted, confessed, “We have sinned against the LORD,” and Samuel judged them there.
Did you know? When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, they went up against them, and the Israelites were afraid of them.
Did you know? At Israel’s request, Samuel prayed to the LORD on their behalf and offered a whole lamb as a burnt offering.
Did you know? As Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines, throwing them into confusion, and they were defeated by Israel.
Did you know? The Israelites went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines as far as below Beth-car.
Did you know? Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen and named it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”

Did you know? Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life. Each year he went around to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, then returned to Ramah, where his home was and where he built an altar to the LORD.
